j.n: This config maps count-less <kbd>j</kbd>/<kbd>k</kbd> to <kbd>gj</kbd>/<kbd>gk</kbd> (display lines); <kbd>5j</kbd> still moves 5 real lines

w.d: Forward to start of next word
w.n: word = letters, digits, underscore (or a run of other non-blanks); WORD = anything up to whitespace

W.d: Forward to start of next WORD (blank-delimited)
W.n: WORD = any run of non-blank characters, e.g. foo.bar(baz) is one WORD

ge.d: Back to end of previous word

gE.d: Back to end of previous WORD

0.d: To first column of the line

^.d: To first non-blank character of the line

$.d: To end of line (with N: end of line N-1 lines down)
$.n: In Visual block mode <kbd>$</kbd> extends every line to its own end

g_.d: To last non-blank character of the line (N-1 lines down)

gg.d: To first line, or to line N

G.d: To last line, or to line N

N%.d: To N percent through the file

%.d: Jump to the matching bracket, or to the next bracket on the line
%.n: matchit (loaded by default) also jumps between if/else/endif, HTML tags and similar pairs; see <kbd>g%</kbd>, <kbd>[%</kbd>, <kbd>]%</kbd>

H.d: To top line of the window (Nth line from top)

M.d: To middle line of the window

L.d: To bottom line of the window (Nth line from bottom)

f.d: To Nth {char} to the right on this line

F.d: To Nth {char} to the left on this line

t.d: Till before Nth {char} to the right

T.d: Till after Nth {char} to the left

;.d: Repeat last f/t/F/T in the same direction

,.d: Repeat last f/t/F/T in the opposite direction

bar.d: To column N of the line

-.d: Up N lines, on first non-blank

+.d: Down N lines, on first non-blank

<CR>.d: Down N lines, on first non-blank (same as +)

CTRL-M.d: Same as <CR>: down N lines, first non-blank

_.d: To first non-blank, N-1 lines down (linewise)

g0.d: To first character of the screen line

g^.d: To first non-blank of the screen line

g$.d: To last character of the screen line

gm.d: To middle of the screen width

gM.d: To middle of the text line (N percent with a count)

go.d: To byte N in the buffer

[[.d: Back to previous section ('{' in column 1)

]].d: Forward to next section ('{' in column 1)

[].d: Back to previous section end ('}' in column 1)

][.d: Forward to next section end ('}' in column 1)

[m.d: Back to start of a method (Java/C++ style class)

]m.d: Forward to start of the next method (Java/C++ style class)

[/.d: Back to start of a C comment /*

]/.d: Forward to end of a C comment */

star.d: Search forward for the whole word under the cursor
star.n: Whole-word match (\<word\>); 'ignorecase' applies, 'smartcase' does not. In Visual mode Neovim's default * searches for the selected text instead

#.d: Search backward for the whole word under the cursor

gstar.d: Like * but also matches inside longer words

g#.d: Like # but also matches inside longer words

n.d: Repeat last search in the same direction
n.n: <kbd>n</kbd> follows the direction of the last / or ?, so after <kbd>?</kbd> it goes backward

N.d: Repeat last search in the opposite direction
N.n: Opposite of the last search direction, not always 'backward'

/.n: Case-sensitive in this config ('ignorecase' off); add \c to the pattern to ignore case. Search offsets: /foo/e end, /foo/+1 next line

/<CR>.d: Search forward again with the last pattern

?<CR>.d: Search backward again with the last pattern

gn.d: Select next match of the last search (cgn + . changes them one by one)
gn.n: Works as a text object: <kbd>cgn</kbd> changes the next match, then <kbd>.</kbd> repeats on the next one

gN.d: Select previous match of the last search

gd.d: Go to local declaration of the word (searches back in the function)
gd.n: This config maps <kbd>gd</kbd> to the Snacks LSP definitions picker

gD.d: Go to global declaration of the word (searches from top of file)
gD.n: This config maps <kbd>gD</kbd> to the Snacks LSP declarations picker

CTRL-C.d: Interrupt the current command or search

[I.d: List lines containing the word under cursor (also in included files)

]I.d: List lines containing the word under cursor, starting at the cursor

[i.d: Show first line containing the word under cursor (incl. included files)

]i.d: Show first line below the cursor containing the word

[_CTRL-I.d: Jump to first line containing the word under cursor

]_CTRL-I.d: Jump to first line below the cursor containing the word

[D.d: List #defines matching the word under cursor
[D.n: Neovim remaps this key to diagnostic navigation; the #define search is only reachable via :normal!

]D.d: List #defines matching the word under cursor, starting at the cursor
]D.n: Neovim remaps this key to diagnostic navigation; the #define search is only reachable via :normal!

[d.d: Show first #define matching the word under cursor
[d.n: Neovim remaps this key to diagnostic navigation; the #define search is only reachable via :normal!

]d.d: Show first #define below the cursor matching the word
]d.n: Neovim remaps this key to diagnostic navigation; the #define search is only reachable via :normal!

[_CTRL-D.d: Jump to first #define matching the word under cursor

]_CTRL-D.d: Jump to first #define below the cursor matching the word

<S-LeftMouse>.d: Extend the selection to the mouse click
<S-LeftMouse>.n: Neovim's default 'mousemodel' is popup_setpos; only with extend does it search the clicked word like *

<S-RightMouse>.d: Search backward for the word at the mouse click (like #)

d.n: This config maps d, D, c, C, x, X to "d…: deleted text goes to register d, not the clipboard. Paste it with "dp

c.d: Change: delete {motion} text and start Insert
c.n: Deleted text goes to register d in this config (see d)

y.n: With 'clipboard' = unnamedplus, yanks go to the system clipboard ("+)

!.d: Filter {motion} lines through an external command

gq.n: When an LSP attaches, Neovim sets 'formatexpr' to the LSP formatter if it was empty

gw.d: Format {motion} lines and keep the cursor where it was

o_v.d: Force the operator to work charwise (e.g. dvj)
o_v.n: Also toggles inclusive/exclusive for charwise motions: <kbd>dve</kbd> leaves the last char

o_V.d: Force the operator to work linewise (e.g. dVw)

o_CTRL-V.d: Force the operator to work blockwise

D.d: Delete to end of line (and N-1 more lines)

C.d: Change to end of line (and N-1 more lines)

Y.d: Yank N lines (Neovim maps Y to y$: yank to end of line)
Y.n: Neovim default mapping Y → y$ (like D and C); use yy for whole lines

p.d: Put (paste) after the cursor N times
p.n: With 'clipboard' = unnamedplus, p pastes the system clipboard. Deletes go to "d in this config, so use "dp to paste deleted text

P.d: Put (paste) before the cursor N times
P.n: Unlike <kbd>p</kbd>, <kbd>P</kbd> in Visual mode keeps the register, so you can paste repeatedly

gp.d: Put after the cursor and leave the cursor after the pasted text

gP.d: Put before the cursor and leave the cursor after the pasted text

]p.d: Put after, adjusting indent to the current line

[p.d: Put before, adjusting indent to the current line

!!.d: Filter N lines through an external command

x.d: Delete N characters under and after the cursor
x.n: Mapped to "dx here: the character goes to register d

X.d: Delete N characters before the cursor

s.d: Delete N characters and start Insert

S.d: Delete N lines and start Insert (same as cc)

gR.d: Enter Virtual Replace mode (overtype screen cells, tabs stay intact)

gr.n: Neovim's <kbd>grn</kbd>/<kbd>gra</kbd>/<kbd>grr</kbd>/<kbd>gri</kbd>/<kbd>grt</kbd>/<kbd>grx</kbd> LSP maps extend <kbd>gr</kbd>, so it waits for 'timeoutlen' before acting

J.d: Join N lines (default 2) with one space
J.n: In Visual mode joins the selected lines

gJ.d: Join lines without inserting or removing spaces

CTRL-A.d: Increment the number at or after the cursor by N
CTRL-A.n: Works on decimal, 0x hex, 0b binary and (with 'nrformats') letters; <kbd>g<C-a></kbd> in Visual makes a sequence

CTRL-X.d: Decrement the number at or after the cursor by N

<MiddleMouse>.d: Paste at the mouse position (like gP)

<Del>.d: Delete N characters under the cursor (same as x)

i.n: A count repeats the inserted text: <kbd>3ihey<Esc></kbd> → heyheyhey

I.d: Insert at first non-blank of the line

gI.n: This config maps <kbd>gI</kbd> to the Snacks LSP implementations picker

gi.d: Insert where Insert mode was last stopped

o.d: Open a new line below and start Insert

O.d: Open a new line above and start Insert

u.n: 'undofile' is on in this config, so undo history survives closing the file

U.d: Undo all recent changes on the last changed line (is itself undoable)

..d: Repeat the last change (a count replaces the original count)
..n: Repeats inserts too: <kbd>A;<Esc></kbd> then <kbd>j.</kbd> appends ; to the next line

&.d: Repeat last :s on the current line (Neovim: same flags, :&&)
&.n: Neovim default mapping & → :&&<CR> keeps the last flags (Vim's plain & drops them)

g&.d: Repeat last :s on all lines with the same pattern and flags

g-.d: Go to older text state (walks undo branches by time)

g+.d: Go to newer text state (walks undo branches by time)

@:.d: Repeat the last command-line command N times
@:.n: After the first <kbd>@:</kbd>, <kbd>@@</kbd> repeats it again

v_o.d: Move the cursor to the other end of the selection

v_O.d: Block mode: move to the other corner on the same line

v_b_I.d: Block mode: insert the same text before the block on every line
v_b_I.n: Type the text, then <kbd><Esc></kbd>: it appears on every line of the block

v_b_A.d: Block mode: append the same text after the block on every line

v_gv.d: Swap the current and previous Visual areas

v_v.d: Switch to charwise Visual, or stop Visual mode

v_V.d: Switch to linewise Visual, or stop Visual mode

v_CTRL-V.d: Switch to blockwise Visual, or stop Visual mode

v_CTRL-G.d: Toggle between Visual and Select mode

v_CTRL-O.d: Select mode: switch to Visual mode for one command

gV.d: In a Select-mode mapping: don't reselect the area afterwards

<RightMouse>.d: Open the right-click popup menu (moves the cursor to the click)
<RightMouse>.n: Neovim's default 'mousemodel' is popup_setpos; with extend it starts or extends Visual mode instead

v_c.d: Change the selection (delete and start Insert)

v_C.d: Change the selected lines (block: to end of each line)

v_D.d: Delete the selected lines (block: to end of each line)

v_p.d: Replace the selection with the register (old text goes to the unnamed register)
v_p.n: The replaced text goes to the unnamed register, so a second <kbd>p</kbd> pastes the old text; use <kbd>P</kbd> to keep pasting the same thing

v_P.d: Replace the selection with the register (registers unchanged)

v_gJ.d: Join the selected lines without spaces

v_!.d: Filter the selected lines through an external command

v_CTRL-A.d: Increment numbers in the selection by N

v_CTRL-X.d: Decrement numbers in the selection by N

v_g_CTRL-A.n: Select a column of 0s and press <kbd>g<C-a></kbd> to number them 1, 2, 3…

v_:.d: Start a command line with the range '<,'> of the selection

m.d: Set mark {a-zA-Z} at the cursor (A-Z are global, across files)
m.n: Special marks: . last change, ^ last insert, " last exit, [ ] last change/yank, < > last selection

'.d: Jump to the line of mark {a-zA-Z0-9} (first non-blank)

`.d: Jump to the exact position of mark {a-zA-Z0-9}

''.d: Jump back to the line before the latest jump

``.d: Jump back to the position before the latest jump

CTRL-O.d: Jump to an older position in the jump list
CTRL-O.n: Jumps are made by G, /, n, %, (, {, marks, etc. — not by j/k or w

CTRL-I.d: Jump to a newer position in the jump list
CTRL-I.n: Shadowed here: this config maps <Tab> (Sidekick NES, no fallback) and <C-i> is not mapped separately, so per :h CTRL-I the <Tab> map also catches <C-i>, even in kitty or Neovide; use <leader>sj

<Tab>.d: Jump to a newer position in the jump list (same as CTRL-I)
<Tab>.n: This config maps Normal-mode <kbd><Tab></kbd> to Sidekick NES jump/apply (no fallback)

g;.d: Go to an older position in the change list
g;.n: Change list = positions of your edits; <kbd>:changes</kbd> lists them

g,.d: Go to a newer position in the change list

`[.d: To start of the last changed, yanked or put text

`].d: To end of the last changed, yanked or put text

'[.d: To first line of the last changed, yanked or put text

'].d: To last line of the last changed, yanked or put text

`<.d: To start of the last Visual selection

`>.d: To end of the last Visual selection

'<.d: To first line of the last Visual selection

'>.d: To last line of the last Visual selection

g'.d: Jump to mark without adding to the jump list (line)

g`.d: Jump to mark without adding to the jump list (exact position)

['.d: To previous line with a lowercase mark

]'.d: To next line with a lowercase mark

quote.d: Use register {x} for the next delete, yank or put
quote.n: "" unnamed, "0 last yank, "1-9 deletes, "+ clipboard, "_ black hole, "/ search, ": last command. In this config d/c/x default to "d but honour a register you type (except "+)

@.d: Run the macro in register {a-z} N times
@.n: Macros are just registers: <kbd>"ap</kbd> pastes one to edit, <kbd>"ayy</kbd> stores it back

@@.d: Repeat the last executed macro (or @:) N times

Q.d: Replay the last recorded macro N times
Q.n: Neovim: <kbd>Q</kbd> replays the last recorded register (Vim's Ex mode is <kbd>gQ</kbd>). In linewise Visual it runs on every selected line

CTRL-D.d: Scroll half a screen down (N lines with a count)

CTRL-U.d: Scroll half a screen up (N lines with a count)

CTRL-E.d: Scroll the view N lines down (text moves up, cursor stays)

CTRL-Y.d: Scroll the view N lines up (text moves down, cursor stays)

zz.d: Scroll so the cursor line is centered

zt.d: Scroll so the cursor line is at the top

zb.d: Scroll so the cursor line is at the bottom

z<CR>.d: Cursor line to top of window, cursor on first non-blank

z..d: Cursor line to center of window, cursor on first non-blank

z-.d: Cursor line to bottom of window, cursor on first non-blank

zh.d: Scroll the view N characters left (nowrap only)

zl.d: Scroll the view N characters right (nowrap only)

zH.d: Scroll the view half a screen width left (nowrap only)

zL.d: Scroll the view half a screen width right (nowrap only)

zs.d: Scroll horizontally so the cursor is at the left edge (nowrap only)

ze.d: Scroll horizontally so the cursor is at the right edge (nowrap only)

<PageDown>.d: Scroll one screen forward (same as CTRL-F)

<PageUp>.d: Scroll one screen back (same as CTRL-B)

i_CTRL-X_CTRL-E.d: Scroll the window one line down (like CTRL-E) in CTRL-X mode

i_CTRL-X_CTRL-Y.d: Scroll the window one line up (like CTRL-Y) in CTRL-X mode

CTRL-W_S.d: Split the window horizontally (same as s)

CTRL-W_w.d: Go to the next window (wraps); with N: go to window N
CTRL-W_w.n: Most CTRL-W keys also work with CTRL held for the second key: <kbd><C-w><C-w></kbd>

CTRL-W_h.d: Go to the window on the left

CTRL-W_l.d: Go to the window on the right

CTRL-W_p.d: Go to the previous (last accessed) window

CTRL-W_q.d: Quit the window (like :quit; quits Neovim if it is the last)

CTRL-W_c.d: Close the window (like :close; never closes the last one)

CTRL-W_=.d: Make all windows (almost) the same size

CTRL-W__.d: Maximize window height (or set it to N)

CTRL-W_bar.d: Maximize window width (or set it to N columns)

CTRL-W_+.d: Increase window height by N lines

CTRL-W_-.d: Decrease window height by N lines

CTRL-W_>.d: Increase window width by N columns

CTRL-W_<.d: Decrease window width by N columns

CTRL-W_x.d: Swap with the next window (or window N)

CTRL-W_H.d: Move the window to the far left (full height)

CTRL-W_J.d: Move the window to the very bottom (full width)

CTRL-W_K.d: Move the window to the very top (full width)

CTRL-W_L.d: Move the window to the far right (full height)

CTRL-W_T.d: Move the window to a new tab page

CTRL-W_n.d: Open a new window with an empty buffer

CTRL-W_f.d: Split and edit the file name under the cursor

CTRL-W_F.d: Split, edit the file under the cursor and go to its line number

CTRL-W_gf.d: Edit the file name under the cursor in a new tab

CTRL-W_].d: Split and jump to the tag under the cursor

CTRL-W_}.d: Show the tag under the cursor in the preview window

CTRL-W_^.d: Split and edit the alternate file (or buffer N)

CTRL-W_d.d: Split and jump to the #define of the word under the cursor
CTRL-W_d.n: Neovim remaps <kbd><C-w>d</kbd> / <kbd><C-w><C-d></kbd> to show diagnostics in a float

CTRL-W_i.d: Split and jump to the declaration of the word under the cursor

za.d: Toggle the fold under the cursor

zA.d: Toggle the fold under the cursor recursively

zo.d: Open the fold under the cursor

zO.d: Open all folds under the cursor recursively

zc.d: Close the fold under the cursor

zC.d: Close all folds under the cursor recursively

zR.d: Open all folds (set 'foldlevel' to the deepest)

zr.d: Open one more fold level everywhere ('foldlevel' + 1)

zm.d: Close one more fold level everywhere ('foldlevel' - 1)

zv.d: Open just enough folds to show the cursor line

zx.d: Reset folds to 'foldlevel', then show the cursor line

zj.d: Move down to the start of the next fold

zk.d: Move up to the end of the previous fold

[z.d: Move to the start of the current open fold

]z.d: Move to the end of the current open fold

zf.d: Create a fold over {motion} (manual / marker folding)

zF.d: Create a fold for N lines

zd.d: Delete the fold under the cursor

zD.d: Delete folds under the cursor recursively

zE.d: Delete all folds in the window

z=.d: Spelling suggestions for the word under the cursor
z=.n: Needs 'spell' on (:set spell); a count picks suggestion N directly

zg.d: Add the word to the spell file as correct

zw.d: Add the word to the spell file as wrong

zG.d: Mark the word correct for this session only

zW.d: Mark the word wrong for this session only

zug.d: Undo zg (remove the word from the spell file)

]s.d: Move to the next misspelled word

[s.d: Move to the previous misspelled word

do.d: Diff: obtain the change from the other window (:diffget)

dp.d: Diff: put the change into the other window (:diffput)

]c.n: Not remapped here: gitsigns is set up without keymaps, so <kbd>]c</kbd>/<kbd>[c</kbd> only move between diff changes

CTRL-].d: Jump to the definition (tag) of the word under the cursor
CTRL-].n: When an LSP client attaches, Neovim sets 'tagfunc', so <kbd><C-]></kbd> goes to the LSP definition and <kbd><C-t></kbd> comes back

CTRL-T.d: Jump back up the tag stack

g].d: List all tags matching the word under the cursor (:tselect)

g_CTRL-].d: Jump to the tag, or list matches if there are several (:tjump)

v_CTRL-].d: Jump to the tag of the selected text

<C-LeftMouse>.d: Jump to the tag of the word at the mouse click

<C-RightMouse>.d: Jump back up the tag stack (same as CTRL-T)

gf.d: Edit the file whose name is under the cursor

gF.d: Edit the file under the cursor and jump to the line number after it

gx.d: Open the file path or URL under the cursor with the system handler
gx.n: Neovim maps gx (Normal and Visual) to vim.ui.open(): URLs, paths, LSP document links; in help files, help tags

CTRL-G.d: Show the file name, line count and cursor position

g_CTRL-G.d: Show cursor position plus word, character and byte counts

ZZ.d: Write if changed and close the window (like :x)

CTRL-Z.d: Suspend Neovim (resume with fg in the shell)

[f.d: Edit the file under the cursor (same as gf)

]f.d: Edit the file under the cursor (same as gf)

CTRL-^.d: Switch to the alternate (previous) buffer; with N: buffer N
CTRL-^.n: The quickest way to toggle between two files

gt.d: Go to the next tab page (with N: tab page N)

gT.d: Go to the previous tab page

g<Tab>.d: Go to the last accessed tab page

CTRL-<Tab>.d: Go to the last accessed tab page

<C-Tab>.d: Go to the last accessed tab page

K.d: Look up the keyword under the cursor with 'keywordprg'
K.n: This config maps <kbd>K</kbd> to LSP hover

v_K.d: Look up the selected text with 'keywordprg'

i_<Help>.d: Leave Insert mode and open the help window

CTRL-L.d: Redraw the screen (Neovim default: also clears search highlight)

ga.d: Show the character code under the cursor (decimal, hex, octal)
ga.n: This config's <kbd>gai</kbd>/<kbd>gao</kbd> (LSP calls) make <kbd>ga</kbd> wait for 'timeoutlen'

g8.d: Show the UTF-8 bytes of the character under the cursor

g<.d: Show the output of the previous command again

count.d: Count: repeat or scale the next command (3w, 5dd, 2p)

N<Del>.d: While typing a count: remove its last digit

CTRL-\\_CTRL-N.d: Go to Normal mode (no-op in Normal mode; useful in mappings)

CTRL-\\_CTRL-G.d: Go to Normal mode (no-op in Normal mode)

g.d: Extended command prefix (gg, gu, gq, gv, gx …)

z.d: Fold / scroll / spell command prefix (za, zz, z= …)

N:.d: Start an Ex command with the range .,.+(N-1)

q:.d: Open the command-line window with : history (edit and re-run)
q:.n: In this config <kbd><CR></kbd> in Normal mode starts Leap here; press <kbd>i</kbd> then <kbd><CR></kbd> to run the line

q/.d: Open the command-line window with / search history

q?.d: Open the command-line window with ? search history

gQ.d: Enter Ex mode (keep entering : commands; :vi to return)

<LeftMouse>.d: Move the cursor to the mouse click

v_iw.n: Text objects work after an operator (<kbd>diw</kbd>, <kbd>ci"</kbd>, <kbd>yap</kbd>) or in Visual mode; <kbd>i</kbd> = inner, <kbd>a</kbd> = around

v_aw.d: A word, plus surrounding white space
v_aw.n: <kbd>daw</kbd> deletes the word and one space, so the sentence stays tidy

v_aW.d: A WORD, plus surrounding white space

v_ap.d: A paragraph, plus the following blank lines

v_a(.d: ( ) block including the parentheses (same as ab)

v_a).d: ( ) block including the parentheses (same as ab)

v_a{.d: { } block including the braces (same as aB)

v_a}.d: { } block including the braces (same as aB)

v_at.d: XML/HTML tag pair including the tags

i_CTRL-C.d: Leave Insert mode without abbreviations or InsertLeave
i_CTRL-C.n: Skips InsertLeave autocmds, which plugins may rely on; prefer <kbd><Esc></kbd>

i_CTRL-R_CTRL-R.d: Insert register literally (keys like <BS> in it are not applied)

i_CTRL-R_CTRL-P.d: Insert register literally and fix the indent

i_CTRL-W.d: Delete the word before the cursor
i_CTRL-W.n: Neovim default: sets an undo point first, so <kbd>u</kbd> can bring the text back

i_CTRL-U.d: Delete text typed before the cursor (if none, all text before it)
i_CTRL-U.n: Neovim default: sets an undo point first, so <kbd>u</kbd> can bring the text back

i_CTRL-H.d: Delete the character before the cursor (same as <BS>)

i_<BS>.d: Delete the character before the cursor

i_<Del>.d: Delete the character under the cursor

i_CTRL-O.d: Run one Normal-mode command, then return to Insert

i_0_CTRL-D.d: Delete all indent of the current line

i_CTRL-A.d: Insert the text from the last Insert session

i_CTRL-@.d: Insert the text from the last Insert session and leave Insert

i_CTRL-E.d: Insert the character below the cursor

i_CTRL-Y.d: Insert the character above the cursor

i_CTRL-V.d: Insert the next key literally (e.g. a real <Tab>)

i_CTRL-Q.d: Insert the next key literally (same as CTRL-V)

i_CTRL-V_digit.d: Insert a character by code: 065, x41, u20ac, o101

i_CTRL-G_u.d: Start a new undoable change (undo break)

i_CTRL-G_U.d: Don't start a new undo step for the next cursor movement

i_CTRL-G_j.d: Down a line, to the column where Insert started

i_CTRL-G_k.d: Up a line, to the column where Insert started

i_CTRL-].d: Expand an abbreviation without typing a character

i_<Tab>.n: In buffers where blink.cmp is attached, <Tab> tries in order: next snippet placeholder, Sidekick next-edit suggestion, accept Copilot ghost text, else a normal Tab (lua/plugins.lua:331-340)

i_CTRL-N.n: With blink.cmp's menu closed, <kbd><C-n></kbd>/<kbd><C-p></kbd> open blink's menu instead (first / last item selected). <kbd><C-x><C-n></kbd> still runs built-in keyword completion

i_CTRL-X.d: Enter CTRL-X completion mode (next key picks the source)

i_CTRL-X_CTRL-O.d: Omni completion ('omnifunc'; LSP when a client is attached)
i_CTRL-X_CTRL-O.n: Neovim sets 'omnifunc' to vim.lsp.omnifunc when an LSP attaches

i_CTRL-X_CTRL-N.d: Complete keywords from the current buffer (forward)

i_CTRL-X_CTRL-P.d: Complete keywords from the current buffer (backward)

i_CTRL-X_CTRL-I.d: Complete keywords from current and included files

i_CTRL-X_CTRL-Z.d: Stop completion, keep the typed text

c_CTRL-R.d: Insert a register; <C-r><C-w> word, <C-r><C-a> WORD, <C-r><C-l> line
c_CTRL-R.n: <kbd>:%s/<C-r><C-w>/</kbd> pre-fills a substitute for the word under the cursor

c_CTRL-R_CTRL-O.d: Insert a register or cursor object literally

c_<Tab>.d: Complete the command or argument before the cursor
c_<Tab>.n: In this config blink.cmp handles command-line completion: <kbd><Tab></kbd> opens its menu and inserts the first match (accepts a lone match), then cycles; <kbd><C-n></kbd>/<kbd><C-p></kbd> move, <kbd><C-y></kbd> accepts

c_CTRL-N.d: Next completion match, else next (newer) history entry

c_CTRL-P.d: Previous completion match, else older history entry

c_<Up>.d: Older history entry starting with the typed text

c_<Down>.d: Newer history entry starting with the typed text

c_CTRL-W.d: Delete the word before the cursor

c_CTRL-B.d: Cursor to start of the command line

c_CTRL-E.d: Cursor to end of the command line

c_CTRL-D.d: List completions matching the text before the cursor

c_CTRL-L.d: Insert the longest common part of the matches

c_CTRL-G.d: While typing a search: go to the next match ('incsearch')

c_CTRL-T.d: While typing a search: go to the previous match ('incsearch')

c_CTRL-V.d: Insert the next key literally (or a character code)

c_CTRL-\\_e.d: Replace the command line with the result of {expr}

:buffer.d: Go to buffer N, or by (partial) name with Tab completion

:bdelete.d: Unload a buffer and remove it from the list (closes its windows)
:bdelete.n: This config's <kbd><leader>bd</kbd> uses Snacks.bufdelete, which keeps the window layout

:bufdo.d: Run a command in every listed buffer

:bwipeout.d: Wipe a buffer completely (marks, options, everything)

:delmarks.d: Delete marks (:delm a b, :delm! for all lowercase)

:keepjumps.d: Run a command without changing the jump list

:registers.d: Show register contents (:reg a b for specific ones)
:registers.n: Register d holds deletes in this config

:global.d: Run an Ex command on every line matching {pattern}: :g/pat/cmd
:global.n: :g/TODO/d deletes matching lines; :g/^/m0 reverses the file

:vglobal.d: Run an Ex command on every line NOT matching {pattern}: :v/pat/cmd

:normal.d: Run Normal-mode keys, on each line of [range]: :%norm A;
:normal.n: Use :normal! to ignore mappings (this config remaps d, c, x, j, k, s …)

:source.d: Run a Vim script or Lua file (:so % runs the current file)

:write.d: Write the buffer to its file (or to {file})

:quit.d: Close the window; exits Neovim when it is the last one

:xit.d: Write only if changed, then close the window

:edit.d: Edit {file}; with no argument, reload the current file

:substitute.n: Flags: g all on line, c confirm, i/I case, n count only. & in {string} = whole match, \1 = group

:sort.d: Sort lines in [range] (n numeric, i ignore case, u unique, r /pat/)

:earlier.d: Go back in undo time: :earlier 10m, :earlier 3f (file writes)
:earlier.n: 'undofile' is on in this config, so this reaches back across sessions

:later.d: Go forward in undo time (counterpart of :earlier)

:undolist.d: List the leaves of the undo tree

:make.d: Run 'makeprg' and load errors into the quickfix list

:cdo.d: Run a command on each quickfix entry: :cdo s/a/b/ | update

:cfdo.d: Run a command once per file in the quickfix list

:ldo.d: Run a command on each location-list entry

:lfdo.d: Run a command once per file in the location list

:windo.d: Run a command in every window

:argdo.d: Run a command on every file in the argument list

:new.d: Open a new window with an empty buffer

:vnew.d: Open a new vertical window with an empty buffer

:tabnew.d: Open a new tab page (optionally editing {file})

:tabedit.d: Edit {file} in a new tab page

:tabnext.d: Go to the next tab page

:tabprevious.d: Go to the previous tab page

:tabmove.d: Move the tab page to position N (or +N / -N)

:nohlsearch.d: Clear search highlighting until the next search

:cwindow.d: Open the quickfix window only if there are entries

:cnext.d: Go to the next quickfix entry

:cprevious.d: Go to the previous quickfix entry

:colder.d: Go to the older quickfix list

:cnewer.d: Go to the newer quickfix list

:vimgrep.d: Search files into the quickfix list: :vim /pat/ **/*.lua

:grep.d: Run 'grepprg' and load matches into the quickfix list

:saveas.d: Save to {file} and make it the current file

:update.d: Write only if the buffer was modified

:wqall.d: Write all modified buffers and quit

:xall.d: Write all modified buffers and quit

:t.d: Copy lines (same as :copy): :t. duplicates a line

:put.d: Put a register linewise below the line (above with :put!)

:lcd.d: Change the working directory for this window

:tcd.d: Change the working directory for this tab page

:!.d: Run a shell command; with a range, filter the lines through it

:=.d: Print the last line number; := {expr} evaluates Lua (like :lua =)

:set.d: Show or set options (:set wrap?, :set nowrap, :set sw=4)

:setlocal.d: Set an option for this buffer/window only

:map.d: Show or create mappings (:map with no args lists them)

:verbose.d: Run a command verbosely; :verbose map x shows where x was set

:diffthis.d: Add this window to the diff

:diffget.d: Get the change from the other diff buffer

:diffput.d: Put the change into the other diff buffer

:&.d: Repeat the last :substitute (:&& keeps the flags)

:restart.d: Restart Neovim, restoring the session (:restart! does not)

:mksession.d: Save the session (windows, buffers) to a file

:noautocmd.d: Run a command without triggering autocommands

:silent.d: Run a command without showing messages

:filter.d: Filter the output of a listing command: :filter /pat/ ls

:redir.d: Redirect messages to a file, register or variable

:vertical.d: Make the following split vertical: :vert help x

:tab.d: Open the following command's window in a new tab: :tab help x

n|q{0-9a-zA-Z\"}.n: Press <kbd>q</kbd> again to stop; then <kbd>@a</kbd> plays it, <kbd>@@</kbd> / <kbd>Q</kbd> repeat

n|~.d: Toggle case of N characters and move right

n|~{motion}.d: Toggle case of {motion} text (only when 'tildeop' is set)

c|<C-F>.d: Open the command-line window to edit the command
c|<C-F>.n: Edit the command with Normal-mode keys. In this config <kbd><CR></kbd> in Normal mode starts Leap, so press <kbd>i</kbd> then <kbd><CR></kbd> to run the line

i|<C-L>.d: Completion menu: insert one more character from the current match

i|other.d: Completion menu: any other key stops completion and inserts itself

n|g<MiddleMouse>.d: Paste at the mouse click (same as <C-MiddleMouse>)

entries.d: Leave Terminal mode for Normal mode (scroll, search, yank output)
entries.n: Every key except <kbd><C-\></kbd> goes to the job. Snacks terminals also accept a quick double <kbd><Esc></kbd>

entries.d: Run one Normal-mode command, then return to Terminal mode
Send {char} to the job (the <C-\> itself is not sent)
entries.n: Only <kbd><C-n></kbd> and <kbd><C-o></kbd> after <kbd><C-\></kbd> are handled by Neovim; <kbd><C-\><C-\></kbd> sends one <kbd><C-\></kbd>

entries.d: Enter Terminal mode (keys go to the shell / job)
entries.n: a, I, A and :startinsert do the same. Snacks terminals re-enter Terminal mode automatically when you switch back to them

entries.d: Enter Terminal mode (same as i)
Jump to the previous shell prompt

entries.d: Jump to the next shell prompt
Leave Terminal mode (two quick presses, within 200 ms)
entries.n: A single <kbd><Esc></kbd> is still sent to the program (e.g. to leave vi-mode in the shell)

entries.d: Hide the terminal window (job keeps running)
entries.n: Set in lua/plugins.lua (Snacks terminal win keys). From Normal mode the global <kbd><C-/></kbd> toggles it back; <kbd>2<C-/></kbd> opens a second terminal

notes.title: The grammar: operator + count + motion
notes.lead: Most editing is a sentence: a verb (operator) applied to a noun (motion or text object).
rows: indent the inside of a { } block
doubling the operator acts on the whole line
notes.note: Learn one new operator and it works with every motion you already know.

notes.title: Counts and the dot
notes.lead: A number in front repeats or scales; <kbd>.</kbd> repeats the last change.
rows: all the same: the count can go before the operator or the motion
5 real lines down (relative numbers are on in this config)
go to line 4 · go halfway through the file
repeat the last change · repeat it with count 3
change the word under the cursor, then each next match
record a macro, replay it 10 times (<kbd>Q</kbd> replays the last one)

notes.title: Registers in this config
notes.lead: Put <kbd>"</kbd>{reg} before a yank, delete or put to choose where text goes.
rows: 'clipboard' is unnamedplus: yank and put use the system clipboard
mapped to "d…: deleted text lands in register d, the clipboard stays clean
black hole register: in this config it is overridden by the "d mapping, use :normal! "_d…
insert a register in Insert or Command-line mode
notes.note: Because d/c/x are mappings that prepend "d, any register you type before them is replaced by d (checked: "adiw fills "d, not "a).
